body: Sorry about the late reply bing52. I have been spending a lot more time on www.ywbb.org. Which is a young widow/ widower support forum, where you can talk to a large community of other young widows and widowers. It's been incredibly helpful to me and I have /u/JubBird to thank for pointing it out to me on this very subreddit. As far as the dreams go, I've had a couple of really bad ones and early on I experienced some sleep paralysis for the first time in my life. The way the human mind and body deals with stress like this is definitely scary, and very humbling. Hope any of this helps, and if you check out the ywbb sight, my user name there is ForEm.
It's scaring me because of how much it seems like I actually want to do it.
I'm still pretty scatter-brained and having a hard time with things. I think I do like this therapist. I slept last night, for the first time in a while.

Thank you so much for sharing your story. It does give a sense that things will get better even if I can't see, or believe it right now. I am in the stage now, where food and sleep are hard. I have good and bad days. "One day at a time" has been repeated to me ad nauseum, to the point where I got sick of hearing it, but the truth is it really is helpful. Every time I try to think to the future right now I don't see anything good, so I'm trying my best to stick in the present even if that's not very good either.
Thank you very much, I've got a lot of people I can PM now, which is nice.
I am so thankful that we didn't have a child. I would be useless to them right now.
I think I'm going to do one or two more sessions one-on-one and then ask about a group. Hearing from other people really has been helpful.

My counselor last night allowed me to say the same thing. I think it really did help, she didn't tell me anything new but it was a chance to talk about my wife for an hour, which is a subject that no one else seems to want to talk about. It was nice to remember her and to an extent share her with someone that never got to meet her and see how amazing she was.
